method: Codex source inspection and mathematical scope check; no external-model ideation or review.

checks.hypothesis: An allowed input operation could preserve the complete deterministic forecast/cost function while changing the action derivative used by native gradient planning.
source_findings: The optional Adam configuration names stable_worldmodel.solver.GradientSolver, AdamW, 30 steps, 100 samples and learning rate 0.1.
Action encoding, autoregressive prediction and terminal latent MSE retain a differentiable action path. The clone/detach of initial encoded observations does not detach subsequent candidate actions.

The actual solver implementation and a qualified local LeWM checkpoint/Clean run were not established by this inspection. Default task configurations use CEM. No end-to-end backward or planning run was performed.
checks.mathematical_boundary: If two differentiable deterministic scalar costs agree on an action neighborhood, their action derivatives agree there. Equality only at a finite set of cached actions does not establish equality of the functions. Custom backward or detach-based derivative replacement grants control over the backward program and does not, by itself, identify a new restricted input attack.
checks.decision: Do not launch a LeWM gradient experiment on this hypothesis. A reachable restricted operation, compatible competent controller and distinction from archived gradient mechanisms remain missing.
checks.scope: Rejects this proposed justification, not gradient-based planning research in general.

checks.hypothesis: CEM's final elite average can be executed without the same acceptance decision applied to sampled candidates.
source_findings: DINO forecasts the newly updated mean on every CEM iteration and saves predicted_best_encs. The code then returns its prefix without scoring and accepting/rejecting that forecast. It is incorrect to say this mean is never forecast.

NanoWM returns the final elite mean without an additional final-mean rollout. Earlier means enter the next iteration as candidate zero. Its recorded final_loss is the last iteration's best sampled loss, not necessarily the returned mean's cost.
Existing final-mean caches do not provide the real outcomes of all final elites, so they cannot establish that safe elites were averaged into a dangerous action.
checks.decision: Do not treat ordinary multimodal averaging risk as a new security mechanism without a distinct constrained intervention. Preserve the existing strong-CEM CartPole return tie of 200/200; no new task experiment is justified by these source differences alone.
checks.scope: Source semantics only. No claim that final-mean synthesis is always safe or that a two-returned-mean diagnostic reconstructs the complete native candidate bank.
